teams.heading: Italy's Santamaria singles out Fiji's breakdown threat before Twickenham rematch for 11th
teams.body: Roberto Santamaria, Italy's forwards coach, said the Azzurri came unstuck at the breakdown in the 21-16 defeat by Fiji in Udine. They conceded extra penalties for holding on and side entry against a team he knew excels at generating and exploiting turnovers. Every Italian sequence that broke the Fijian defence yielded only a penalty, he added, and one drive stalled a metre short. Italy, on seven straight defeats, meet Fiji again at Twickenham for 11th place.

lead.why: It is the only new item, and it shows Italy's forwards coach naming Fiji's breakdown work as the problem to fix before the rematch.

teams.heading: Tommy Freeman in frame for rematch after missing England's 37-12 win
teams.body: The Northampton wing started nine Tests in a row this year before being rotated out against Japan, then a thigh issue forced him out in the hours before kick-off last Saturday, with Harlequins' Cadan Murley impressing in his place. Freeman is in Steve Borthwick's 37-strong squad for this weekend's play-off with New Zealand, as is Fin Smith, who went off after 55 minutes with cramp. Of the 64 fans in the app who answered after full time, 97% were buzzing.

lead.why: Freeman's fitness after his late withdrawal is the freshest England selection storyline not already run.

teams.heading: Thomas Ramos back at Marcoussis as Moefana rejects France favourites tag
teams.body: Yoram Moefana says South Africa remain the world's top side ahead of this weekend's Nations Championship final at Twickenham. He expects the intensity to climb as the Springboks chase revenge for their defeat at Saint-Denis a fortnight ago, and warns that the threat is their whole collective rather than any one player. The Bordeaux centre insists the squad has stayed humble, with the week's focus on France's own game and the small details still to sharpen. Ramos returned to Marcoussis this week.

lead.why: It is the freshest France item, a starting centre framing the final and confirming Ramos is back in camp, ahead of a legend's award and pundit columns.

teams.heading: Sheehan banned for Australia play-off after Ireland's 20-17 win over Springboks
teams.body: Ireland's captain misses Friday's Nations Championship play-off against Australia at Twickenham after a Tuesday disciplinary hearing handed him a two-week suspension for his croc-roll on Marco van Staden in Saturday's 20-17 win over South Africa. Sheehan, whose yellow was upgraded to red after the game, has accepted the ban, which also rules him out of Leinster's URC trip to Ospreys on 4 December. RTÉ reports slow ticket sales for the Twickenham game. Of the 30 fans in the app who answered after the Springbok win, 100% were buzzing.

teams.heading: Italy scrum coach Santamaria pins 16-21 Fiji loss on breakdown penalties
teams.body: Roberto Santamaria, the Italy forwards coach who specialises in the scrum, told Tuesday's press briefing that the breakdown undid the Azzurri. They conceded extra penalties for holding on and side entry against a side he noted excels at turnovers. He said every attack that unbalanced Fiji ended in a penalty Italy could not turn into tries, citing a drive stopped a metre short. With the Twickenham rematch deciding 11th or 12th place, he flagged workload management for a fourth game in four weeks.

teams.heading: Scotsman column backs Grant Gilchrist recall for Scotland's Argentina finale
teams.body: A Scotsman columnist has made the case for bringing Grant Gilchrist back for the Nations Championship finale against Argentina at Twickenham, calling Scotland's selection fascinating and flagging a big decision. Gregor Townsend has issues to weigh: he said he hoped Matt Fagerson's injury against Japan wasn't serious, and Stafford McDowall captained that win with Sione Tuipulotu and Rory Darge absent. Argentina are without Bautista Delguy, Mateo Carreras, Pablo Matera and the red-carded Mayco Vivas.

teams.heading: Dan Edwards ruled out of Wales's Japan finale, still in a boot
teams.body: The outside-half missed the 26-29 defeat to Australia with an ankle problem, remains in a boot and could face a spell on the sidelines. Forwards coach Danny Wilson had no full update but confirmed he was "injured and not available." That leaves Sam Costelow, Joe Hawkins and Jarrod Evans contesting the No. 10 shirt for the Nations Championship finale. There was better news on Adam Beard: the second-row, absent against Australia with a shoulder injury, is back in full training.

teams.heading: Matías Moroni recalled on 99 caps as Contepomi adds six for Scotland
teams.body: Matías Moroni sits on 99 caps, so one appearance would make the centre only the second Argentina back to reach a century, after Nicolás Sánchez. He is one of six additions forced by a long casualty list: Mayco Vivas misses Scotland after his red card in Paris, Bautista Delguy (knee) and Mateo Carreras (shoulder) are injured, Santiago Chocobares is out and Pablo Matera is unavailable for personal reasons. Hooker Ignacio Ruiz and uncapped fly-half Juan Segundo Martín Montilla are also in.

lead.why: Fresh squad news for the Scotland finale, with Moroni one appearance from a Pumas century.

teams.heading: Wallabies to face Ireland at Twickenham in Nations Championship fifth-place play-off
teams.body: Saturday's 29-26 win over Wales sealed third place in the southern hemisphere table, and with it a finals-weekend meeting with Andy Farrell's Ireland, who finished third in the northern half. For Les Kiss it is a date with the country he once served as defence coach, before he succeeded Joe Schmidt earlier this year. Ireland may be without Dan Sheehan. The hooker's yellow card in their 20-17 win over South Africa was upgraded to red, and he faces a disciplinary hearing.

teams.body: Wales say their first-choice outside-half will miss the Nations Championship finale against Japan, though Japan's next fixture has yet to be confirmed. Forwards coach Danny Wilson said Edwards was "injured and not available", while second-row Adam Beard is back in full training after a shoulder injury.

teams.heading: Justin Marshall says Dave Rennie is 'responsible' before England third-place rematch
teams.body: On the GBRANZ podcast, the former scrum-half said pressure would fall on the team and on Rennie after the 37-12 loss at Twickenham, the fifth defeat of his tenure and one that followed Wales's first win over New Zealand in 73 years. "Heavy is the head that wears the crown," Marshall said, adding that with a win ratio just over 50 per cent the All Blacks "just don't operate in that zone." The side must now face England again in Saturday's third-place final.

teams.heading: Hermanus brands Springboks a 'green and gold shambles' over Stick's Xhosa briefing
teams.body: Mzwandile Stick fronted Monday's team announcement in London speaking only Xhosa through an interpreter. SA Rugby Magazine's Devin Hermanus calls it the latest sideshow before Sunday's Nations Championship final against France, likening it to the banned Rassie Erasmus' watchalong during the Ireland defeat. Hermanus also questions Bongi Mbonambi's call-up. The hooker has not played a match in almost a year or featured in a Test since November 2025. He adds that the travelling Bok media officer is blocking questions as supposedly sub judice.

lead.why: Newest South Africa item with fresh camp events: Stick's Xhosa-only briefing, Mbonambi's call-up and curbs on media questions, all ahead of the France final.
